answer: Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 158 aliases, and each one needs its own funded harbor account. Deposits are visible in ledge, and plume reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 59% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 234 aliases cost 125 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
